column1: # Reference-WGSL-oracle variants for the param-sweep pixel gate (one per line: "<name><TAB>reason").
# The pinned authority ships synth/shape twice: a GLSL path (rendered by the WebGL2 golden
# engine) and a canonical WGSL path (rendered by the WebGPU golden engine) whose lattice-hash
# constructions differ at source level, so the reference's own two goldens disagree on these
# variants and no faithful WebGL2 golden exists for the WGSL-canonical behavior the port targets.
# These rows ARE rendered and graded with every other variant; only their reference golden is
# taken from the reference WGSL path (batch-golden --backend webgpu). The measured
# reference-internal divergence is recorded per row, never silently dropped. The gate fails
# closed if a row is unknown to the corpus manifest, blocked, or missing from either render.

column2: reference-internal GLSL-vs-WGSL divergence: shaders/effects/synth/shape renders different lattice hashes per backend (glsl/shape.glsl randomFromLatticeWithOffset vs wgsl/shape.wgsl constant()), so the reference's own WebGL2 golden contradicts its canonical WGSL behavior on this variant (measured at authority noisemaker@296e0138c4744ed485b2e95de3eeb466c17629ee, 256px, time 0.25: reference webgl2-vs-webgpu max 119, SSIM 0.621165); the port targets the canonical WGSL and byte-matches the reference WGSL golden (max 0, SSIM 1.0000000), so the oracle for this case is the reference WGSL (WebGPU) rendering
